CVE-2026-119078.title: Apache Commons Codec: Blake3 doFinalize is stateless; the documented KDF example derives identical keys
CVE-2026-119078.description:
Apache Commons Codec's Blake3 class documented the output of its doFinalize methods as depending on any previously finalized bytes, so that consecutive calls would return different output. In fact, doFinalize does not change the hash state: calling it again without supplying more input returns the same bytes. The key-derivation example in the class Javadoc, shipped since 1.16.0, derives two keys with two consecutive doFinalize calls. Code that follows it gets identical keys, so the separation between the derived keys is lost. The same applies to any application that calls doFinalize more than once on one instance and expects new output each time.

This issue affects Apache Commons Codec from 1.16.0 before 1.23.0.

Version 1.23.0 corrects the documentation, but the behavior of doFinalize is unchanged. Upgrading alone does not fix affected code. Users should check their applications for repeated doFinalize calls on the same Blake3 instance and derive multiple keys by requesting the…

CVE-2026-119193.title: PHPUnit vulnerable to code execution by other local users via shared temporary directory in PHPT code coverage handling
CVE-2026-119193.description: PHPUnit is a testing framework for PHP. From 13.4.0 until 13.4.4, the TestCase::coverageFilesDirectory() logic in src/Runner/Phpt/TestCase.php creates temporary files for PHPT code coverage in a predictable phpunit-phpt directory under sys_get_temp_dir() and reuses that directory without verifying its ownership or permissions. On multi-user systems with a shared temporary path, a local attacker who creates the directory before the developer runs PHPT tests with code coverage can replace the generated job file before the child process executes it with require, allowing arbitrary code execution with the developer's privileges while the test and coverage report appear successful. PHPUnit 12.5 and earlier, default macOS and Windows configurations with per-user temporary directories, and single-user environments where another user cannot create files in the temporary path are not affected. This issue is fixed in 13.4.4.

CVE-2026-120539.description: The Restrictions for BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This is due to the plugin splicing the attacker-controlled request URI into a PHP expression inside a double-quoted string and evaluating it with eval(). CVE-2026-98937.title: perf/core: Check kernel access when kernel callchains are requested
CVE-2026-98937.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

perf/core: Check kernel access when kernel callchains are requested

perf_event_open() currently gates perf_allow_kernel() only on
!attr.exclude_kernel.

However, users can still request kernel callchain collection with
attr.exclude_callchain_kernel == 0 even when attr.exclude_kernel == 1.
That still requires kernel profiling privilege, but the existing check
does not enforce it.

Update the permission check to call perf_allow_kernel() when either
kernel sampling is requested or kernel callchains are requested.

This keeps permission checks aligned with requested data and prevents
unprivileged use of kernel callchain capture.

CVE-2026-99026.title: net: team: free skb when broadcast has no txable port
CVE-2026-99026.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: team: free skb when broadcast has no txable port

bc_transmit() sends the original skb through the last txable port.
When no port is txable, it returns false without consuming the skb, but
team_xmit() still returns NETDEV_TX_OK. AF_PACKET sends then retain the
skb and its socket write-memory charge.

A TX-enabled, link-down port keeps the broadcast transmit op installed.
Carrier can stay up through a second link-up, TX-disabled port or be
forced on by userspace. Free the original skb on the no-port path while
leaving the existing drop accounting intact.

Discovered by Sashiko during review of previous commit.

CVE-2026-99480.title: drm/panthor: Fix TOCTOU race between GROUP_REGISTERED check and erase
CVE-2026-99480.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/panthor: Fix TOCTOU race between GROUP_REGISTERED check and erase

panthor_group_destroy() checks the GROUP_REGISTERED mark and then calls
xa_erase() without holding the xarray lock across both. If the handle is
destroyed by another thread in between, and a concurrent GROUP_CREATE
reuses the freed ID, the first destroy erases and releases the new,
still-initializing group, leading to a use-after-free in
panthor_group_create().

Do the mark check and erase atomically under xa_lock().

CVE-2026-99589.title: batman-adv: tt: clear ROAM flag when re-adding a pending local client
CVE-2026-99589.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

batman-adv: tt: clear ROAM flag when re-adding a pending local client

When a ROAMING_ADV is received for an announced local client,
batadv_tt_local_mark_removed() sets BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM, queues a
DEL|ROAM change and marks the entry as BATADV_TT_CLIENT_PENDING. If the
client sends a frame again before the next TTVN commit,
batadv_tt_local_add_existing() only clears the PENDING flag and returns
early. The ADD cancels the queued DEL, but the entry keeps the ROAM flag:

* batadv_is_my_client() reports the client as not served by this node
* batadv_tt_local_client_is_roaming() reroutes unicast frames for it to
the node which sent the ROAMING_ADV

The ROAM flag is only removed with the next frame of the client.

Since BATADV_TT_CLIENT_ROAM is set together with BATADV_TT_CLIENT_PENDING,
it has to be cleared also at the same time with BATADV_TT_CLIENT_PENDING
when the client roamed back.
